definitions.explanation: A set phrase said after finishing a meal to express gratitude. Literally related to {馳走|ちそう} meaning 'feast' or 'to run around (preparing food).'

examples.japanese: ごちそうさま⟦でした→です：09485_desu⟧。
ごちそうさま！⟦おいしかった→美味しい：00740_oishii⟧。
examples.english: Thanks for the meal! It was delicious.

examples.japanese: ⟦{食|た}べ→食べる：00396_taberu⟧⟦{終|お}わったら→終わる：00567_owaru⟧、ごちそうさま⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}いましょう→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: When you finish eating, let's say 'gochisousama.'

examples.japanese: ⟦とても→とても：00593_totemo⟧⟦おいしかった→美味しい：00740_oishii⟧⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧。ごちそうさま⟦でした→です：09485_desu⟧。
examples.english: It was very delicious. Thank you for the meal.

examples.japanese: ⟦お{母|かあ}さん→お母さん：02851_okaasan⟧、ごちそうさま。⟦{今日|きょう}→今日：00496_kyou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦カレー→カレー：02898_karee⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{本当|ほんとう}に→本当：00779_hontou⟧⟦おいしかった→美味しい：00740_oishii⟧⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧。⟦また→また：00969_mata⟧⟦{作|つく}って→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧。
examples.english: Mom, thanks for the meal. Today's curry was really delicious. Please make it again.

notes: ごちそうさま (casual) or ごちそうさまでした (polite) is said after eating, expressing thanks to whoever provided or prepared the meal. The word {馳走|ちそう} historically referred to running around to gather ingredients to prepare a feast for guests. It's paired with ⟦いただきます→いただきます：00946_itadakimasu⟧ before meals.
